exercise.title: Why do the constant and identity formulas match their graphs?

statement.p: A constant function has derivative 0, and the identity function x has derivative 1. In your own words, why are those the only numbers that could appear, even before the limit calculation is written down?

hint.p: A horizontal line has no change. The line y=x rises one output unit for each input unit.

exercise.title: Why does the power rule drop the exponent as a coefficient?

statement.p: For a positive integer n, the difference quotient of x^n becomes a sum of n terms, each approaching x^{n-1}. In your own words, why does that produce the formula nx^{n-1}, and why was the case n=0 already handled by constants?

hint.p: Count the terms after factoring out h. The expression nx^{n-1} with n=0 would formally contain a negative power, even though the derivative of the constant 1 is simply 0.

exercise.title: Why differentiate first and then evaluate?

statement.p: A formula such as p'(x)=30x^5-6x^2+7 describes slopes along the whole graph, while p'(1) is one slope at one point. In your own words, why must the function be differentiated before a particular input is substituted, and what do these first formulas still not cover?

hint.p: Substituting first would freeze the graph at one height and destroy the rate information. Products, quotients, and compositions need later rules.

subsection.title: What we have proved so far
subsection.p: These rules are enough to differentiate every polynomial.

statement.p: Each term is handled separately. The constant 8 contributes nothing to the derivative because it does not affect change.

subsection.title: What these formulas do not yet cover
subsection.p: The rules in this section are useful, but they are not enough for most functions.
They do not yet tell us how to differentiate
These functions are built not only by adding and scaling, but also by multiplying, dividing, and putting one function inside another.

The next chapter develops the algebra of derivatives. The goal is not to memorize more rules for their own sake. The goal is to make the derivative practical while keeping its meaning: a local rate of change, a tangent slope, and the coefficient of the best linear approximation.
